body:
To clarify, the simplest reproduction looks like (captured in the linked reproduction):
```html
<md-chip-list>
  <md-chip *ngFor="let item of list>...</md-chip>
</md-chip-list>

<md-input-container>
  <input mdInput [(ngModel)]="someValue">
</md-input-container>
```
Where the constructor for `MdInput` has
```ts
  constructor(private _elementRef: ElementRef,
              private _renderer: Renderer2,
              @Optional() @Self() public _ngControl: NgControl,
              @Optional() private _parentForm: NgForm,
              @Optional() private _parentFormGroup: FormGroupDirective) {
```

The problem **only** happens when:
* The input has an `NgModel` applied
* The chip is on the same element as `NgFor`
* The `list` iterated over by `NgFor` changes after `OnInit`
* `MdInput` injects `FormGroupDirective` with `@Optional` **and** `private`


My best guess is that having a decorator on a private member somehow triggers a code path that corrupts the injector for the view (since the chips are siblings/cousins to the input)

rename.from: Using @Optional() private causes wrong Renderer to be injected
rename.to: JIT: Using @Optional() private causes wrong Renderer to be injected

body:
I've got the same issue, though my reproduction ([plunker link](https://plnkr.co/edit/z5SGnEDdd6NhpFVG1GZA)) is slightly different

```html
<form myForm>
  <my-form-group>
    <my-form-element>
      <input type="checkbox" [(ngModel)]="checked" name="foo">
      <my-validation *ngIf="!checked">foo</my-validation>
    </my-form-element>
  </my-form-group>
</form>
```

with the `MyValidation` constructor

```typescript
constructor(renderer: Renderer2, elementRef: ElementRef) {
  console.log('validation:', renderer);
}
```

This results in

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/821510/27377497-6c2a4a06-5675-11e7-9647-56ac35143b18.png)

It took me a while to get this reproduction running, because there are a lot of conditions before this issue arises:

- the `[myForm]` component must be present on the form element
- the `*ngIf` must be present on the validation component
- the `[(ngModel)]` must be present on the input
- the `ElementRef` must be injected in the `MyValidationComponent` constructor
- the `providers` mustn't be empty in the `MyFormElementComponent`'s `@Component` metadata
- the `<my-form-group>` element must be in the template

Change any one of these conditions and suddenly the correct `Renderer2` is injected.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/821510/27378000-cfbeeb5c-5676-11e7-862d-379caae43a48.png)

There are no private properties in my reproduction, though I do use constructor arguments that aren't public properties.
